solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Chest sound of annoying concertgoer

indicators.note: the clue asks for how a word is pronounced, not how it is spelt

parts.note: someone who coughs through a quiet passage is a cougher

explanation.surface: Someone at a concert notices the noise coming from the chest of a nuisance in the next seat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chest' looks like the source of the cough; it is the definition, a strongbox.
explanation.definitionFit: A coffer is a strongbox, a chest for keeping money or valuables.

clue.text: Time for love in works of graphic art or pottery

indicators.note: X for Y means X takes the place of Y in the word

parts.note: comics are stories told in drawn pictures
love is nil in tennis, the letter O
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: Someone wonders about substituting time for love in comic strips or in making pots.
explanation.walkthrough: In COMICS, ERA replaces the O.
explanation.definitionFit: Ceramics is the craft of making objects from fired clay, which covers pottery.

clue.text: The Greatest adipose coating causing death

indicators.note: one word wraps around the other, covering it like a layer

parts.note: adipose tissue is fatty tissue
Muhammad Ali called himself The Greatest

explanation.surface: A grim medical picture of a boxing champion done in by a layer of body fat.
explanation.definitionFit: A fatality is a death caused by an accident or disaster.

clue.text: Man discovering bird's nest, finally

parts.note: the erne is the sea eagle, a crossword favourite; with 's it gives the possessive

indicators.note: only the closing letter of the word nest is wanted

explanation.surface: A man finds where a bird has been nesting at last.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernest is a man's first name, so it can stand for a man.

clue.text: Immature person carrying weapon to port

indicators.note: the first word holds the second within it, as one carries a load

parts.note: a youth is a young person
an arm is a weapon, as in firearm

explanation.surface: A young man takes a gun down to the harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: Great Yarmouth is a Norfolk port on England's east coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Yarmouth is an English seaside town with a harbour, an example of a port.

clue.text: Save a rising Semite

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means the letters are read from the bottom up

parts.note: save means except, as does bar

explanation.surface: An instruction to rescue a member of a Semitic people who is getting up.
explanation.definitionFit: Arabs are a Semitic people, alongside Jews and others speaking Semitic languages.

clue.text: Think to behave dipomatically? About time!

indicators.note: the first word goes around the other, enclosing it

parts.note: to mediate is to act as a diplomatic go-between

explanation.surface: An exasperated cry that someone is finally thinking about being tactful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About time!' reads as an exclamation; 'About' is the container and 'time' the T it holds. 'Dipomatically' is the clue's own typo for diplomatically.
explanation.definitionFit: To meditate is to ponder or reflect deeply, a synonym of think.

clue.text: Eradicate, or put round about

indicators.note: about signals the letters are moved around into a new order

parts.note: a round shape is the letter O

explanation.surface: Instructions to wipe something out or simply move it around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' is a ring shape, the letter O, which joins the pool that 'about' shuffles.
explanation.definitionFit: To uproot is to pull up by the roots, hence to eliminate entirely.

clue.text: Scam leaves saint and student in shade

indicators.note: the pieces are placed inside the other word

parts.note: a hue is a shade of colour
L for learner, as on British learner-driver plates

explanation.surface: A con trick sees a holy man and a pupil left in the dark.
explanation.definitionFit: A hustle is a fraud or swindle, another name for a scam.

clue.text: A US compound's inverted membrane

indicators.note: turned upside down, so the letters are read in the opposite order

parts.note: niter is the American spelling of nitre, potassium nitrate

explanation.surface: A chemistry note about an American compound whose membrane has been turned over.
explanation.definitionFit: The retina is the light-sensitive layer of tissue lining the back of the eye.

clue.text: Shakespearean animals (black and white) adopting sport

indicators.note: the first word takes the other in, as a family takes in a child

parts.note: giant pandas are black-and-white bears
RU is rugby union

explanation.surface: Zoo pandas take up a game.
explanation.definitionFit: Pandarus is a character in Shakespeare's Troilus and Cressida, the go-between of the lovers.

clue.text: Academic gathering returning artist to French city

indicators.note: going back, so the letters are read in reverse order

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician
Nimes is a city in southern France

explanation.surface: A painter heading home to a French city for a conference.
explanation.definitionFit: A seminar is a class or meeting for discussion at a university.

clue.text: Spies eating idiot's treacle

indicators.note: the first word takes the second inside it

parts.note: moles are spies planted inside an organisation
an ass is a fool; the 's is the possessive

explanation.surface: Agents tucking into a fool's sweet syrup.
explanation.definitionFit: Molasses is the American word for the dark syrup called treacle in Britain.

clue.text: Ramble resulting in introduction to school bully

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word school

parts.note: a troll is an online bully

explanation.surface: A walk that leads to a child meeting a schoolyard tormentor.
explanation.definitionFit: A stroll is a leisurely walk, as is a ramble.

clue.text: Plan to plug school with messy mark

indicators.note: one word fills a gap in the other, like a stopper

parts.note: a plot is a scheme or plan

explanation.surface: A scheme to block up a school leaves a stain.
explanation.definitionFit: A splotch is a blot or smudge, an untidy patch of colour.

clue.text: Pretty snub nose, finally

parts.note: to snub someone is to cut them dead

indicators.note: only the closing letter of the word nose

explanation.surface: A charming upturned nose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'snub nose' reads as one phrase; split it.
explanation.definitionFit: Cute means attractive in a sweet way, close to pretty.

clue.text: Place in wrong side of argument

indicators.note: the word goes inside the other letters
the letters are put wrongly, out of order

parts.note: to place is to put

explanation.surface: Someone claims a thing was set on the wrong side of a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' scrambles the four letters of 'side' to DISE, and 'in' sets the word for Place inside that.
explanation.definitionFit: A dispute is a disagreement or quarrel, an argument.

clue.text: Underworld scotched a Stuart monarch

indicators.note: scotched means ruined, so the letters are thrown out of order

parts.note: R for rex or regina, king or queen

explanation.surface: History: the hell of a Stuart king being thwarted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scotched' rearranges A, STUART and R (from 'monarch'); the Stuarts were a Scottish royal house, hence the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: Tartarus is the deepest pit of the underworld in Greek myth.

clue.text: Wire one on limping nag, initially, into this paper

indicators.note: the pieces are placed inside the other word

parts.note: FT is the Financial Times, where the puzzle appears
I is the Roman numeral for one
a limping animal is lame

indicators.note: only the first letter of nag

explanation.surface: A racing tip wired in to the paper about a lame horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A filament is a fine thread or wire, as in a light bulb.

clue.text: Ooze involving sort of beauty, say

definitions.note: describing a quality, e.g. beauty; an adjective

indicators.note: one word wraps up the other within it

parts.note: to seep is to ooze
a kind is a sort

explanation.surface: Seepage from a certain kind of beauty treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort' also leads the definition: beauty, the saying goes, is only skin-deep.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says beauty is only superficial, merely on the surface.

clue.text: Exemplar to knock back old sporting event

indicators.note: knock back reads as drink, but back alone tells us to read the word for knock from end to start

parts.note: to rap is to knock
an agon was a contest in ancient Greek games

explanation.surface: A model of how to defeat an ancient sports contest.
explanation.definitionFit: A paragon is a model of excellence, a perfect example.

clue.text: Flower power popular with king

parts.note: P is the symbol for power in physics
in means fashionable, popular
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: Flower power goes down well with the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinks are garden flowers of the carnation family.

clue.text: Detective's dodgy 8

indicators.note: dodgy means unsound, so the letters are moved around

parts.note: the number points to the solution of 8 down

explanation.surface: A detective's crooked accomplice.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleuth is a detective, from sleuth-hound, a tracking dog.

clue.text: What average Spanish gent?

parts.note: par is the normal or average level
Don is a Spanish title for a gentleman

explanation.surface: A query about how ordinary a Spanish gentleman is.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are polite requests for someone to repeat themselves.

clue.text: Kiss during love duet damaged waistcoat

indicators.note: the word sits within the other letters
the letters are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: love is nil, the letter O
X is a written kiss

explanation.surface: A smooch in the middle of a romantic duet left a waistcoat ruined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' rearranges O and DUET into TUEDO; 'during' puts X within it.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuxedo can name a formal dinner suit with its accompanying waistcoat.

clue.text: Fidelity, once — yet all go astray

indicators.note: going astray means wandering off course, so the letters wander out of order

explanation.surface: A lament that faithfulness, once valued, now always goes wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Lealty is an archaic Scottish word for loyalty, hence 'once'.

clue.text: Composer's examination covers smell with note

indicators.note: the first word surrounds the second

parts.note: a scan is a medical examination
hum is British slang for a bad smell

explanation.surface: A composer's medical check-up masks an odour, with a note attached.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Schumann was a German Romantic composer.

clue.text: Class with prior convictions

definitions.meaning: a school class or year group

explanation.surface: A description of a group of pupils who already have criminal records.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a school year group and a criminal record go by this word in Britain.

clue.text: Don't pull hard enough for submerged current?

definitions.meaning: to pull too weakly when towing, split into two words
a current beneath the surface of the sea

explanation.surface: A puzzled tug crew wondering about the current below.
explanation.definitionFit: An undertow is a current under the surface running opposite to the waves.

clue.text: Calm song after sunset needing publicity

indicators.note: needing means lacking, so these letters are removed

parts.note: a serenade is an evening song for a lover
an ad is publicity

explanation.surface: An evening love song that badly needs promotion.
explanation.definitionFit: Serene means peaceful and untroubled, a synonym of calm.

clue.text: Ample range wasting energy in domicile

indicators.note: placed inside the other word

parts.note: a domicile is a home

indicators.note: losing, so the letter is taken out

parts.note: the Andes is a mountain range
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A big mountain range losing energy inside the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wasting' removes E from ANDES, giving ANDS.
explanation.definitionFit: A handsome sum is a generous, sizeable one.

clue.text: Beatle to choose to interrupt cleaner?

indicators.note: the word breaks into the other, splitting it

parts.note: a mop is a cleaning tool
to opt is to choose

explanation.surface: A Beatle picks a moment to cut into a cleaner's work.
explanation.definitionFit: Moptop was the nickname for the shaggy-haired early Beatles.
